state.case_summary:
A man in his 40s presented with:- Gradual hair loss of the eyelashes, eyebrows, beard, and scalp for 4 years- Swelling and painful hand joints for 13 months- Multiple asymptomatic nodules on the upper arms for 40 daysNo fever, analgesia or hypesthesia reported. No previous infections, family history, or personal medical history of autoimmune diseases or psoriasis. Previous treatments for joint symptoms showed no improvements over 1 year.

- Diffuse infiltration of the face with loss of skin creases and diminished facial hair- All joints of both hands were swollen- Multiple asymptomatic nodules without ulceration on upper arms- No decreased sensation to pain, temperature and/or touch- No neuropathic changes found

Laboratory Tests:- Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: 27 mm/h (slightly elevated)- Rheumatoid factor: 70.1 IU/mL (significantly elevated)- Normal results for: C-reactive protein, anticyclic citrullinated peptide, antinuclear antibodies, and globulin levelsImaging Studies:- X-ray and joint ultrasound showed: osteoarthritis, synovitis, flexor tendon tenosynovitis, and bone erosions- Ultrasound revealed: enlarged axillary, cervical, and inguinal lymph nodes and enlarged spleen- Fundus fluorescein angiography showed uveitisPathology:Image Title: Skin biopsy from upper arm noduleImage Description: Diffuse infiltrate of foamy histiocytes in the dermis (hematoxylin-eosin stain)Additional Finding: Numerous acid-fast bacilli present (acid-fast stain)

root.label: Chronic Progressive Multisystem Syndrome with Dermatological and Rheumatological Features
supporting_facts: Gradual hair loss of the eyelashes, eyebrows, beard, and scalp for 4 years
Swelling and painful hand joints for 13 months
Multiple asymptomatic nodules on the upper arms for 40 days
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and rheumatoid factor
Diffuse infiltration of the face with loss of skin creases and diminished facial hair
Enlarged axillary, cervical, and inguinal lymph nodes and enlarged spleen on ultrasound
excluded_candidates: Rheumatoid arthritis: reason ranked lower due to lack of response to previous treatments and presence of nodules
Psoriasis: reason ranked lower due to absence of personal or family history and lack of characteristic skin lesions
salient_findings: hair loss of the eyelashes, eyebrows, beard, and scalp
asymptomatic nodules on the upper arms
diffuse infiltrate of foamy histiocytes in the dermis
